name: Saint Martina
history: A Roman virgin and martyr honoured in the city since early times. Her story, written long after her death, tells that she was the daughter of a consul and was tortured and beheaded for refusing to worship the gods. Her relics were rediscovered in 1634 in an ancient church beside the Forum, and she has long been counted among the patron saints of Rome.
life: Almost nothing about Martina can be known with certainty except that the Roman Church honoured her as a martyr. Her legendary acts place her death in the reign of Alexander Severus in the third century, and describe a young noblewoman who gave her wealth to the poor and endured many torments before she was beheaded. A church dedicated to her stood beside the Forum from at least the seventh century. In 1634, during work on the building, her remains were found, and Pope Urban VIII, who was devoted to her, had the church rebuilt by the painter and architect Pietro da Cortona, who spent his own money on her crypt and was later buried there. Urban also wrote the hymns for her feast in the Breviary. The church of Santi Luca e Martina still stands near the Arch of Septimius Severus. Whatever its details, her story speaks for the many young Christians of Rome who chose Christ over life.
prayerTo: Saint Martina, faithful daughter of the Church of Rome, you loved Christ more than wealth, comfort or life itself. Pray for all who suffer for their faith today, for the city of Rome and its bishop, and for me, that I may hold lightly to the things of this world and hold fast to Christ. Amen.
penance: Tradition says Martina gave her wealth to the poor. Give something today that you would rather keep, and pray for persecuted Christians.
meditation: Her name survived when the details of her life were lost, because she belonged to Christ. What in your life will last when everything else is forgotten?
prayer: O God, Who among the other miracles of thy power have bestowed the victory of martyrdom even upon the weaker sex, graciously grant that we who commemorate the anniversary of the death of blessed N., thy Virgin and Martyr, may come to thee by the path of her example. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
